This sets out where each of [the seven quality principles](../00-principles/index.qmd) comes from
in the standards, and where the playbook puts it into practice.

## Where the principles come from

Five of the seven are GovS 010's own ([GovS 010 section 2](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-analysis-functional-standard--2/government-functional-standard-govs-010-analysis#principles)), so following them is how NHSBSA
meets the standard rather than something extra on top. The third and the seventh are NHSBSA's.

| Principle | Source | Where the playbook applies it |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Analysis answers the right questions | GovS 010 principle 1 and section 5.2 | [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) |
| 2. Using the right methods | GovS 010 principle 2, and the AQuA Book | [Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) |
| 3. At the right time | GovS 010 section 5.5. NHSBSA's own principle | [Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) and [working to a deadline](r15-scoring-the-assurance-level.qmd#working-to-a-deadline) |
| 4. With the right level of quality assurance | GovS 010 principle 4 | [Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) for the level, and [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd) for the improvement |
| 5. Following the right standards | GovS 010 principle 5 | [Which standards apply to you](r8-the-standards-landscape.qmd) for the standards, and [data ethics and personal data](r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd) for the ethics |
| 6. Presented in the right way | GovS 010 principle 3 | [Phase 4, delivery, communication and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) and [uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](r10-uncertainty.qmd) |
| 7. So the right decisions are made | NHSBSA's own principle. It restates the aim of GovS 010 principle 3 | All of the playbook. It is the outcome the other six serve |

: Each principle, where it comes from, and where the playbook applies it

### Which parts of GovS 010 are a requirement, and which are a recommendation {#which-parts-of-govs-010-are-a-requirement}

GovS 010 separates *shall*, a requirement, from *should*, a recommendation. Only three of its
requirements are substantive:

- the principles, which the standard puts as "those engaged in analysis shall ensure" ([GovS 010 section 2](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-analysis-functional-standard--2/government-functional-standard-govs-010-analysis#principles))
- a senior officer accountable for NHSBSA's analysis activities
- analytical roles and accountabilities defined in the governance and management framework, and assigned to people with appropriate seniority, skills and experience

The count of *shall*, the clauses and the meaning of *should* are in
[what is binding](r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd#what-is-binding).

## What each principle means in practice

### 1. Analysis answers the right questions {#principle-1-analysis-answers-the-right-questions}

**An analysis with no agreed margin of error has no threshold to be tested against.** Agree it at
scoping, record it in the analytical plan, design against it, and say at the end what is still
uncertain. [Uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](r10-uncertainty.qmd) is how you measure it,
and [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) is where you agree it.

#### Why this sits in the principles rather than in a method {#why-this-sits-in-the-principles}

Three sources ask for the agreement rather than the measurement. GovS 010 asks for the levels of
quality and certainty required to be agreed and recorded at scoping ([GovS 010 section 5.2](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-analysis-functional-standard--2/government-functional-standard-govs-010-analysis#ICES)). At design, the AQuA Book asks analysts to search the planned analysis for sources of
uncertainty large enough to breach "the acceptable margin of error". Somebody has to have said
what that margin is ([AQuA Book section 7.4](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-aqua-book#treatment-of-uncertainty-in-the-design-stage)). And the
[Uncertainty Toolkit for Analysts](https://analystsuncertaintytoolkit.github.io/UncertaintyWeb/)
gives its whole second chapter to jointly agreeing how uncertainty should be used, before the
analysis is designed. **None of the three is about measuring uncertainty.** They are about agreeing
how much of it the decision can carry, while there is still time to design for it.

### 2. Using the right methods {#principle-2-using-the-right-methods}

Repeatable, independent, grounded in reality, objective, with uncertainty understood and managed,
and answering the original question robustly: that is **RIGOUR**, set out in full in
[what each standard asks for](r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd#rigour-in-full).

### 3. At the right time {#principle-3-at-the-right-time}

Where time is genuinely short, the proportionate answer is a narrower question answered properly.

### 4. With the right level of quality assurance {#principle-4-with-the-right-level-of-quality-assurance}

What a review finds goes into the next piece of work.

## What goes wrong when quality is assumed {#what-goes-wrong-when-quality-is-assumed}

Poor analytical quality is rarely obvious at the time. Four patterns are common, and each is a
process failure rather than a competence failure.

**A figure is quoted without its caveat.** The figure appears in a paper. The caveat that qualified
it sat in an annex and did not travel. A decision is taken on a number that meant something narrower than
the reader thought.

**A one-off becomes a production run.** Work built quickly for a single question turns out to be useful
and is rerun for months. Nobody re-assesses anything, because no single moment felt like a decision.

**Assurance is done but not recorded.** Somebody checked. Nobody can now say what they checked, when,
or what they found. The work cannot be defended, and a practice area cannot be evidenced as
compliant.

**Effort goes to the wrong place.** Low-risk work is over-engineered because that is the only
standard anyone has articulated, while high-risk work is assured thinly because the deadline was short.

Each is what the practices in this playbook are there to catch.

## Where this playbook answers GovS 010 {#where-this-playbook-answers-govs-010}

Three things have to be true of every piece of analysis. The quality and certainty required is
agreed and recorded. The checks that deliver it are proportionate to the risk. And somebody is
accountable for the analysis.

[Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd),
[the checks, by level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#the-checks-by-level) and
[roles and responsibilities](../06-roles/index.qmd) are where the playbook does each of them.
